children: shares rose 6.78% to $193.91 at 9:50 a.m. ET on Friday, November 6, recovering part of Thursday's AI rout, even as three House committee chairmen asked CEO Jensen Huang to attend a closed-door briefing. The bounce is about relief. The letter is about risk. Investors now have to price both.

The request comes from Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast, China Select Committee Chairman John Moolenaar and Intelligence Chairman Rick Crawford. They want Huang to address his interactions with a Megaspeed executive the release describes as a publicly reported PRC intelligence asset, along with NVIDIA's safeguards against foreign espionage. The chairmen asked for a reply by November 11 and proposed a November 18 briefing. The release does not accuse Huang or NVIDIA of wrongdoing, but it frames the issue as a national security concern.

The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 92/100, with Profitability and Momentum at 10/10 and Financial Strength at 9/10, while GF Value is the weak spoke at 2/10. At about 24.5 times trailing earnings, the valuation looks less stretched than the headlines suggest, but a strong score does not remove policy risk. The next test is the briefing: any hint of tighter export or compliance rules could hit NVIDIA's China-related sales.

title: NVIDIA Stocks Rebound 6.78% as Lawmakers Call Jensen Huang to Closed-Door Briefing
